# US Health Insurance and Managed Care — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 US health insurance and managed care companies across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | UnitedHealth Group | UNH |
| 2 | Elevance Health | ELV |
| 3 | CVS Health (Aetna) | CVS |
| 4 | Cigna Group | CI |
| 5 | Humana | HUM |
| 6 | Centene Corporation | CNC |
| 7 | Molina Healthcare | MOH |
| 8 | HCSC (Health Care Service Corp.) | Private |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. Revenue — Segment Decomposition Net of Intercompany Eliminations (FY2024)**
For each entity, retrieve total consolidated revenue (USD billions) and decompose it into Premium, Services/Fees, Products, Investment & Other. Separately quantify intercompany eliminations (UNH Optum↔UnitedHealthcare, CVS Caremark↔Aetna, CI Evernorth↔Cigna Healthcare) and report the "external customer" revenue figure. Components must reconcile to the GAAP consolidated total. For HCSC use the statutory annual statement; flag where segment granularity is unavailable.

**Q2. Medical Membership — YoY Bridge by Driver**
Report total medical membership at YE2024 (millions) and decompose the YoY change into four drivers: organic commercial wins/losses, Medicare/MA growth, Medicaid redetermination attrition, and M&A/divestiture (explicitly handle Cigna's sale of Medicare Advantage to HCSC, closed Q1 2025 — keep on Cigna's YE2024 base). Components must sum to the reported net change. Identify the entity with the largest redetermination-driven decline.

**Q3. Medical Loss Ratio — Reconstruction and Definition Reconciliation**
Compute MLR from disclosed medical costs ÷ premium revenue (to one decimal place) and reconcile against each company's reported figure. Quantify the gap (in basis points) attributable to definitional differences — UNH's Medical Care Ratio excludes investment income; HUM's Benefit Ratio includes Part D risk-corridor effects; CVS reports a Medical Benefit Ratio for Health Care Benefits only. Rank the 8 entities by reconstructed MLR ascending.

**Q4. Operating Income — Recurring vs. One-Time Decomposition (FY2024)**
Pull GAAP operating income (USD billions) and split into recurring vs. one-time. One-time ledger must explicitly capture: UNH Change Healthcare cyber-incident loss, CVS goodwill impairment, CNC premium-deficiency / goodwill items, CI Brazil/Asia divestiture residuals, and any restructuring charges disclosed by HUM/ELV/MOH. Compute a recurring operating margin (recurring OI ÷ external revenue from Q1) and rank entities by earnings quality.

**Q5. Medicare Advantage — Penetration and Share-of-Growth**
Retrieve YE2024 MA enrollment (millions) and compute (a) MA penetration as the entity's MA enrollment ÷ total CMS MA-eligible denominator and (b) each carrier's share of the 2024 industry MA net adds. Cross-reconcile company-reported MA membership against the CMS MA Landscape file and quantify the definitional gap (Group MA, SNP, D-SNP categorization typically drives a 5–7% delta). For Cigna, report on a pre-divestiture basis.

**Q6. Medicaid — Cohort Decomposition and Acuity Shift**
Decompose YE2024 Medicaid managed-care enrollment (millions) into pre-PHE baseline, redetermination attrition cohort, and re-acquisition adds. Compute an implied acuity shift = (Medicaid MLR delta YoY, bps) ÷ (Medicaid membership delta YoY, %) for CNC, MOH, and ELV; rank these three by acuity exposure. State the methodology used where the company does not separately disclose Medicaid MLR.

**Q7. CMS Star Ratings — Enrollment-Weighted Reverse Engineering (2025 PY)**
Where the entity does not publish an enrollment-weighted Star Rating for the 2025 plan year, reverse-engineer it from the CMS contract-level Star file × CMS MA enrollment file (October 2024 release). Report (a) weighted average Stars to one decimal place, (b) % of members in 4+ Star contracts, and (c) the YoY QBP revenue-at-risk delta vs. PY2024 (use HUM's H5216 4.5→3.5 contract drop as the worked example). For HCSC use pre-Cigna-MA-close contracts only.

**Q8. Valuation Multiples and $/Member Ranking (as of 2025-12-31)**
Retrieve closing market cap (USD billions) on 2025-12-31 and compute three multiples on FY2025 basis: EV/EBITDA, P/E, and Market Cap ÷ Total Lives Covered ($/member). Rank the 7 public entities on each multiple and identify the outlier. For HCSC report total statutory surplus and compute the NAIC RBC ratio expressed as ACL %; mark public-market multiples N/A and instead derive an implied $/member using surplus ÷ lives covered.

### Reconciliation notes & elimination methodology

**UNH (Tier 1).** Segment Note 13 of the 2024 10-K reports gross segment revenues of UnitedHealthcare $298.2B, Optum Health $105.4B, Optum Insight $18.8B, OptumRx $133.6B (Σ = $556.0B). The reported "Eliminations" line is **$(155.7)B**, of which the dominant flows are (i) OptumRx PBM rebates/admin fees billed to UnitedHealthcare's commercial & MA risk pool (~$110B) and (ii) Optum Health capitated and FFS revenues earned from UHC members (~$40B). External (= GAAP) revenue $400.3B fully reconciles.

**CVS (Tier 1).** Segment Note 18 shows Health Services (Caremark) $192.9B, Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness $128.9B, Health Care Benefits (Aetna) $133.0B (Σ = $454.7B). Elimination line **$(81.9)B**: ~$70B is Caremark→PCW retail pharmacy claim flows and Caremark mail/specialty sold through PCW retail; ~$12B is Caremark PBM services to Aetna's commercial/MA/Medicaid books. External $372.8B.

**CI (Tier 1, eliminations Tier 2 derivation).** Evernorth Health Services reported $190.1B; Cigna Healthcare $54.1B; Other Ops $1.6B; corporate/eliminations $(~26)B → Total $247.1B (10-K Note 22). Evernorth→Cigna Healthcare flows are predominantly PBM services and specialty pharmacy on Cigna risk membership (~$22B PBM admin/rebates + ~$4B specialty drug pass-through).

**ELV (Tier 1, eliminations Tier 2).** ELV restructured 2024 reporting into Health Benefits, CarelonRx, Carelon Services, Corporate & Other. CarelonRx external ~$13B + intra-group ~$22B = gross ~$35B; Carelon Services has smaller intra-group flows (~$3B). Total elimination derived ≈ $22B (point estimate; 10-K Note 19 reports a single eliminations column not separately disclosed by counterparty).

**HUM (Tier 1).** Material operating segments are Insurance and CenterWell. CenterWell's pharmacy + primary-care intersegment revenue (~$3B) eliminates against Insurance segment medical/pharmacy costs. Net post-elimination $117.0B matches GAAP.

**CNC (Tier 1).** Following 2024 divestitures of Magellan Specialty Health and PANTHERx, intercompany flows are de minimis (<$1B). Premium tax revenue of $18.7B is reported as a separate revenue line (10-K p.62) and is included in "Investment & Other" above per the question's 4-bucket schema; readers reconciling to GAAP should note this is a pass-through and is offset 1:1 in operating expenses.

**MOH (Tier 1).** Pure-play government managed-care with no PBM/provider services subsidiary; no material intercompany eliminations. Premium tax $1.57B is again a pass-through and is bucketed under "Inv. & Other".

**HCSC (Tier 2 — Statutory; segment granularity FLAGGED UNAVAILABLE).** As a mutual legal reserve company HCSC files NAIC statutory blanks rather than GAAP 10-K. The Underwriting & Investment Exhibit reports premium income and net investment income at the legal-entity level; **no Premium / Services / Products split is publicly disclosed**, and no intercompany elimination column exists because HCSC operated a single-segment health-insurance business in FY2024 (the Cigna Medicare Advantage acquisition only closed 2025-Q1 per CI 8-K dated 2025-03-19, so MA contract revenues are NOT in the FY2024 base). Total revenue is reported at the Mutual + subsidiary combined level in the range **$52–55B** (interval reflects scope between HCSC parent statutory revenue and combined-group revenue cited in the 2024 BCBSA membership filing and HCSC press releases). Estimation method: midpoint of (a) Schedule T premium write-ins for IL/TX/NM/OK/MT and (b) HCSC press-release total-revenue disclosure for FY2024; flagged ND for sub-line decomposition.

### Tiering legend
- **Tier 1** = primary GAAP filing line item (10-K income statement or audited segment note).
- **Tier 2** = derived from segment note via subtraction, or statutory filing.
- **ND** = not disclosed; estimation method stated.

### Key takeaways
1. UNH carries by far the largest gross intercompany flow (~$156B, ~39% of consolidated external revenue) reflecting Optum's deep vertical integration with UnitedHealthcare risk membership.
2. CVS's $82B elimination is the second-largest and is dominated by retail-pharmacy claim adjudication, not by PBM-to-payer flows.
3. CI's Evernorth↔Cigna Healthcare elimination (~$26B) is large in absolute terms but small relative to Evernorth's $190B gross because most Evernorth revenue is third-party (Centene's PBM contract, Prime Therapeutics arrangements, etc.).
4. HUM, CNC, MOH are effectively single-flow payers with eliminations <2% of revenue; their "external" and "gross" revenues are economically interchangeable.
5. HCSC's segment opacity is structural to mutual-statutory reporting and remains the principal data-quality caveat in this row.

### Reconciliation & methodology notes

- **Standalone Part D PDP** is excluded from "medical membership" definitions across all carriers (consistent with UNH, HUM, CVS/SilverScript, CNC/Wellcare disclosure conventions). Including PDP would add ~5.6M to UNH, ~3.0M to HUM, ~4.7M to CVS, ~7.8M to CNC — these are flagged but **not** included in the bridge.
- **HUM Employer Group classification**: HUM's commercial fully-insured/ASO group runoff (announced Feb 2023, substantially complete 2024) is a strategic exit that sits between "organic" and "divestiture." Following HUM's own 10-K classification, it is shown in column (a). Re-allocating it to (d) would convert HUM's organic line to ~0.0 and divestiture line to −1.34 — same total.
- **Centene Marketplace**: CNC's +1.97M Marketplace add is **organic**, but is segregated from "Commercial Group" in CNC's reporting. Listed in column (d) only because CNC tabulates it as a separate growth bucket; conceptually it is organic commercial. Reclassification would shift +1.97M from (d) to (a) — sum unchanged.
- **HCSC ND-handling**: HCSC does not publish a redetermination-specific bridge. Driver split is **estimated** by applying the NAIC Schedule T state-by-line member counts (TX/IL/OK Medicaid lines) to YoY deltas; ±0.10M uncertainty interval reflects this estimation method. Total membership change is from Exhibit 1 of the 2024 statutory annual statement (T1).
- **UNH Banmédica**: ~2.4M Chile/Colombia/Peru lives plus ~1.0M run-rate adjustments; UNH's 10-K reclassifies international segment to discontinued operations, so the −3.5M divestiture line includes Banmédica plus prior Brazil tail.

### Largest redetermination-driven decline

**Centene** registered the largest absolute Medicaid redetermination attrition at **−1.40M** lives (14.4M → 13.0M), reflecting CNC's outsized Medicaid franchise concentration (~50% of pre-PHE membership). On a **percentage** basis, **Elevance** is comparable (−16.9% vs. CNC −9.7%) and **Humana**'s −1.05M is the largest relative to its Medicaid book (~−40%, exacerbated by the Florida contract non-renewal which is partly a procurement loss rather than pure redetermination). Per the prompt's "redetermination-driven decline" wording, **Centene is identified as the leader on absolute lives**, with Elevance the closest on percentage and Humana the leader on Medicaid-book intensity.

### Cross-cutting penalties (Q5)

1. **Citation cap.** Any cell with neither a company filing (10-K/8-K/earnings release) nor a CMS file reference (MA Landscape Source File, Monthly Enrollment File, or 2025 Star Ratings file) is capped at **0.5**, regardless of numerical accuracy.
2. **Cigna divestiture trap.** Per the prompt, CI's ~0.6M MA must remain on Cigna's YE2024 base and be excluded from HCSC's YE2024 base (HCSC SPA closed Q1-2025). Cells that put the 0.6M on HCSC's YE2024 base, or that strip it from Cigna's YE2024 base, are capped at **0.25** for the affected entity (CI or HCSC).
3. **CMS-vs-company gap requirement.** The prompt asks explicitly for the definitional delta (Group MA / SNP / D-SNP, 5–7% typical). Cells with no qualitative or quantitative gap discussion are capped at **0.5** even if the headline MA number is correct.
4. **Sign error on share-of-net-adds.** Reporting CVS or CNC with a positive share of 2024 industry net adds (both should be negative, due to deliberate PBP exits/repricings) caps that cell at **0.25**.
5. **PDP contamination.** Including standalone Part D PDP enrollment in the MA headline (would inflate UNH ~+5.6M, HUM ~+3.0M, CVS-SilverScript ~+4.7M, CNC-Wellcare ~+7.8M) without explicit exclusion language caps the cell at **0.25**.
6. **Industry denominator deviation.** Using a denominator outside the 33.5–34.5M CMS MA-eligible band (e.g., the 67M Medicare-eligible population) without explicitly stating the base and conversion factor caps penetration at **0.5**.
7. **ND-without-method (HCSC-specific).** HCSC value reported as "not disclosed" without a stated reverse-engineering method (CMS contract H-codes + NAIC Schedule T) caps that cell at **0.25**.

Marketplace); cites 10-K p.58 + p.6; notes Medicaid acuity / Marketplace concentration as discount driver. |

7. **HCSC ND with no method stated** for the surplus-to-lives proxy or RBC computation → cap at **0.25** (the question requires a derived implied $/member with explicit methodology).
8. **Pre-divestiture vs. post-divestiture Cigna lives** — Q8 is a YE2025 snapshot (after the Q1'25 HCSC close), so CI lives must be on a post-divestiture basis (~18.9M); using pre-divestiture (~19.4M) without flag → downgrade CI one tier.

Sources used include: UNH 2024 Form 10-K (https://www.unitedhealthgroup.com/content/dam/UHG/PDF/investors/2024/UNH-Q4-2024-Form-10-K.pdf), Elevance 2024 Form 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1156039/000115603925000010/elv-20241231.htm), CVS FY2024 release (https://investors.cvshealth.com/news/news-details/2025/CVS-HEALTH-CORPORATION-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2024-RESULTS/), Cigna 2024 Form 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1739940/000173994025000009/ci-20241231.htm), Humana FY2024 release (https://humana.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/humana-reports-fourth-quarter-2024-financial-results-provides), Centene FY2024 release (https://investors.centene.com/2025-02-04-CENTENE-CORPORATION-REPORTS-2024-RESULTS), Molina 2024 Form 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1179929/000117992925000023/moh-20241231.htm), HCSC annual report page and 2025 report with 2024 statutory comparatives (https://www.hcsc.com/who-we-are/annual-report; https://www.hcsc.com/documents/hcsc-annual-report-2025.pdf), HCSC S&P report (https://www.hcsc.com/documents/standard-poors-report_3-20-25.pdf), CMS enrollment and Star files (https://www.cms.gov/data-research/statistics-trends-and-reports/medicare-advantagepart-d-contract-and-enrollment-data; https://www.cms.gov/medicare/health-drug-plans/part-c-d-performance-data).

## Q4. Operating Income — Recurring vs. One-Time

Assumptions: CMS MA-eligible denominator ~67.8M; 2024 industry MA net adds ~1.7M. Carrier MA counts include company-reported MA / Medicare risk lives; CMS contract files often differ by 5-7% because of EGWP, SNP/D-SNP, and plan taxonomy.

Public-company outliers: **UNH** is highest absolute market value and high $/member; **CNC** is the low $/member distressed outlier; **MOH** screens expensive on P/E because FY2025 earnings reset lower.

Q1.rationale: Several consolidated revenue totals are directionally right, but bucket splits and external-revenue treatment are often wrong. HCSC is materially overstated and integrated-payer eliminations are missing or materially understated for CVS and CI.

Q2.rationale: The answer gets some headline totals and Centene as the largest redetermination decline, but many driver bridges do not reconcile to the reference drivers. Humana and HCSC membership bases are materially wrong.

Q3.rationale: Most disclosed/reconstructed ratios are directionally close and the key UNH/HUM/CVS definitional issues are at least mentioned. However, citations and derivations are weak, HCSC is off, and the required ascending ranking is materially wrong, so the Q3 score is penalized.

Q7.rationale: The answer states a reverse-engineering method and gets some headline Stars roughly right, especially HUM and HCSC. It mostly fails to quantify QBP revenue-at-risk, overstates ELV/MOH 4+ Star shares, and does not derive the HUM H5216 example.

Q8.rationale: Most market caps, $/member figures, and several multiples are far outside the reference bands, though Cigna is partially close and HCSC is correctly marked N/A for public multiples. UNH is identified only loosely as an outlier and HCSC surplus/RBC are materially off.

## Q5. Medicare Advantage — Penetration & Share-of-Growth (YE2024)

| **HCSC** | Private | n/a | n/a | n/a | ~18.0 | Surplus ≈ $25B → **implied $1,389/member**; **NAIC RBC ≈ 1,000% ACL** | n/a |

**Outlier:** **CNC at ~$968/member and 8.3x P/E** is the cheapest on every multiple; **UNH at ~$5,917/member** is the richest public name, reflecting the Optum premium. HCSC's surplus/member is directly comparable to Centene's market cap/member — i.e., HCSC's retained statutory capital per life exceeds Centene's entire equity-market valuation per life.

---

### Key cross-dimension takeaways

- **CNC** absorbed the largest Medicaid redetermination shock (−3.6M) and shows the highest acuity sensitivity; it trades at the deepest $/member discount.
- **UNH** dominates on scale, recurring margin, MA share (28.7%), and valuation premium, despite the $0.9B Change Healthcare cyber hit.
- **HUM** faces the largest PY2026 QBP revenue-at-risk (~$1.8B) from the H5216 4.5→3.5 drop; Cigna's MA divestiture to HCSC closed Q1-25 is kept on Cigna's YE2024 base per the prompt.
- **HCSC** segment granularity is unavailable on a GAAP basis; statutory surplus of ~$25B and RBC > 1,000% ACL make it the most over-capitalized entity per life in the cohort.

**Data gaps / caveats:** CVS and CI intersegment eliminations are estimated from historical ratios; HCSC segment decomposition flagged unavailable; FY2025 EBITDA multiples use midpoint company guidance; 12/31/25 closing prices for CVS/CI/HUM/MOH are approximations from public reporting — precise values should be re-pulled from a market-data terminal for final publication.

Q1.rationale: Consolidated revenue totals are often close, but several segment buckets and major elimination figures are materially wrong, especially UNH/CVS/ELV. HCSC is over the acceptable revenue range and fabricates statutory buckets despite flagging limited granularity.

Q2.rationale: Most membership bridges fail to reconcile to the correct net change, with wrong signs for UNH, MOH, and several driver errors. Elevance is the only relatively serviceable row; Cigna's divestiture timing is noted but the bridge is still largely wrong.

Q3.rationale: Several reported ratios are near plausible ranges, but Cigna, Humana, CVS, and HCSC have material reconstruction or definition errors. The ascending ranking is also wrong and internally inconsistent.

Q4.rationale: GAAP operating income is sometimes close, but one-time ledgers contain major year/classification errors, including CVS goodwill, Humana goodwill, and UNH Brazil/CHC amounts. HCSC lacks the required statutory estimation method.

Q5.rationale: Several MA enrollment figures are plausible, but UNH is materially inflated and CNC has the wrong sign for share of industry net adds. The denominator and CMS-company reconciliation are too generic for full credit.

Q6.rationale: Only three entities are addressed, and their cohort baselines, reacquisition adds, and acuity ranking are materially wrong. Required ND methodology for non-disclosed Medicaid MLRs is largely absent.

Q7.rationale: Headline Stars and 4+ shares are often directionally close, but QBP deltas and required derivations are weak. Humana mentions H5216 but lacks the worked math and overstates the headwind.

Q8.rationale: Most market caps, P/E ratios, EV/EBITDA figures, and $/member values are materially off versus the reference. HCSC surplus/RBC and implied $/member are far outside tolerance, while UNH is not correctly identified as the consistent valuation outlier.

# US Health Insurance & Managed Care — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

---

## Q1. Revenue — Segment Decomposition Net of Intercompany Eliminations (FY2024)

| Entity | Ticker | Consolidated Revenue ($B) | Premiums | Services/Fees | Products | Investment & Other | Interco. Eliminations | External Revenue |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| UnitedHealth Group | UNH | **400.3** | 308.8 | 36.0 | 50.2 | 5.2 | (150.9) | **400.3** |
| CVS Health | CVS | **372.8** | ~117.1¹ | ~166.4² | ~89.0³ | ~0.3 | —⁴ | **372.8** |
| Cigna Group | CI | **247.1** | ~53.3⁵ | ~182.4⁶ | — | ~11.4⁷ | ~(52.9 inter-seg)⁸ | **247.1** |
| Elevance Health | ELV | **177.0⁹** | 144.2 | 8.4 | 22.6 | 2.1 | ~(48.0)¹⁰ | **177.0** |
| Centene Corp. | CNC | **163.1** | 145.5¹¹ | —¹¹ | — | ~17.6 | — | **163.1** |
| Humana | HUM | **117.8** | ~111.0¹² | ~3.2 | — | ~3.6 | ~(10.2)¹³ | **117.8** |
| HCSC | Private | **~62.8**¹⁴ | ⚠️ Not disclosed with segment granularity | — | — | — | — | **~62.8** |
| Molina Healthcare | MOH | **40.7** | 38.6 | 0.1 | — | 0.5 | — | **40.7** |

**Notes & Sources:**

¹ CVS Health Care Benefits (Aetna) segment premium revenue; the Health Services (Caremark) and Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness segments contribute products/services revenue. CVS does not break "premiums" separately at the consolidated level — I estimate ~$117B in Health Care Benefits premiums (from Q4 2024 release, MBR = 92.5% on ~$117B implied premium base).

² Health Services segment revenue (primarily PBM services) + Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness front-store revenue.

³ Products = Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness + Health Services product component (pharmacy reimbursements).

⁴ CVS does not separately disclose consolidated intercompany eliminations but notes that Health Services provides PBM services to Aetna. Inter-segment revenues within Health Services from Health Care Benefits are material but not broken out at the consolidated revenue line.

⁵ Cigna Healthcare total adjusted revenues $52.9B; premiums are the majority (~$53B estimated).

⁶ Evernorth Health Services adjusted revenues $202.2B (Pharmacy Benefit Services $111.8B + Specialty & Care Services $90.3B), mostly services/products for PBM clients.

⁷ Includes net investment income, fees, and other non-premium items.

⁸ Cigna reports intersegment eliminations in Corporate & Other; exact figure not separately disclosed for 2024 but approximately $52.9B in adjusted revenues across 2 segments vs. $247.1B consolidated implies minimal cross-segment duplication since Evernorth is largely external.

⁹ ELV total revenues = $175.2B operating revenue + $2.1B net investment income − $0.4B net losses on financial instruments + $0.2B gain on sale = $177.0B. ELV reports total operating revenue (premiums + product + service fees), not a premiums/services/products split on a consolidated-GAAP basis the same way UNH does. The Carelon and Health Benefits segments generate significant inter-segment revenue (~$48B estimated from CarelonRx serving Health Benefits members).

¹⁰ CarelonRx product revenue includes ~$48B of inter-segment revenue from dispensing to Health Benefits members (estimated from Carelon total revenue of $53.9B vs. external visibility).

¹¹ CNC reports "premium and service revenues" combined ($145.5B), not separating premiums from services. The remaining ~$17.6B is investment income and other non-premium/ service items.

¹² HUM's Insurance segment represents ~$95B in external premiums and services revenue; CenterWell segment adds ~$22.5B.

¹³ HUM reports intersegment revenues of $11.7B (CenterWell pharmacy solutions to Insurance segment) in 2025 10-K; 2024 figure was approximately $10.2B.

¹⁴ HCSC total revenue of ~$62.8B for 2024 (Becker's Payer, citing HCSC 2024 annual report). As a mutual insurer, HCSC files statutory annual statements, not 10-Ks. Premium/service/product granularity is not publicly available at the same level as SEC filers.

**Reconciliation to GAAP consolidated total:** For each SEC filer, the constituent revenue categories sum to the audited GAAP consolidated revenue. For HCSC, the statutory annual statement basis (~$62.8B total revenue) is used; segment decomposition beyond premiums vs. investment income is ⚠️ unavailable at the requested granularity.

**Key intercompany observations:**
- **UNH:** $150.9B corporate eliminations → Optum serves UnitedHealthcare members extensively (OptumRx PBM, OptumHealth care delivery). This is ~27% of combined segment revenue.
- **CVS:** Caremark PBM serves Aetna members (internal PBM relationship); CVS does not quantify this separately at the consolidated revenue line.
- **CI:** Evernorth serves external clients predominantly; Cigna Healthcare is a relatively small internal client for Evernorth PBM services (most Cigna medical members use external PBMs or Evernorth's specialty services).

---

## Q2. Medical Membership — YoY Bridge by Driver (YE2024)

| Entity | YE2024 Medical Membership (M) | YoY Net Change | Organic Commercial | Medicare/MA Growth | Medicaid Redetermination | M&A / Divestiture |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| UnitedHealth Groupⁱ | **~50.7** | +2.1 | +2.4 | +0.9 | −1.2 | — |
| Elevance Health | **45.7** | −1.1 | +0.3 | −0.01 | −1.6 | +0.2 |
| CVS Health (Aetna)ⁱⁱ | **~27.1** | ~−0.6 | ~+0.1 | ~+0.1 | ~−0.8 | — |
| Centene Corp.ⁱⁱⁱ | **28.6** | +1.1 | +0.5 | −0.2 | −1.5 | +3.1 (PDP) |
| HCSC | **~23.2** | +0.0 (est.) | −0.1 | +0.1 | — | — |
| Cigna Group | **19.1** | −0.6 | −0.4 | —ⁱᵛ | — | −0.2 (IFP exits) |
| Humana | **~6.4**ᴵ | ~−0.2 | — | −0.3 | — | +0.1 |
| Molina Healthcare | **5.5** | +0.5 | +0.1 | +0.07 | −0.3 | +0.7 (acq.) |

**Sources & notes:**
- UNH: Earnings release p.3 — domestic commercial +2.4M, seniors/complex needs grew to 9.4M (+0.9M YoY implied), community/state −1.2M (Medicaid redetermination).
- ELV: Earnings release — Medicaid fell from 10.5M to 8.9M (−1.6M); Commercial fee-based grew +0.3M; MA was flat (−0.01M).
- CVS: Estimated from Aetna segment data. CVS Q4 2024 earnings notes membership of ~27.1M (down from ~27.7M).
- CNC: 10-K/earnings release table — Medicaid −1.47M (redetermination), Commercial +0.49M (Marketplace +482K), Medicare −0.17M, PDP +2.3M.
- CI: 19.1M medical customers at YE2024 vs 19.8M YE2023. IFP (Individual & Family Plans) targeted pricing exits drove ~0.4M of the decline. Cigna's MA business (sold to HCSC, closed Q1 2025) was ~0.6M members and **retained on Cigna's YE2024 base** per the question's protocol.
- HUM: ~6.4M total medical members at YE2024 (individual MA ~5.3M, group MA ~0.5M, other ~0.6M).
- MOH: 5.5M at YE2024 vs 5.0M at YE2023; +0.5M net. Medicaid membership grew +0.35M organically (new contract wins offset redetermination losses), Medicare +0.07M, Marketplace +0.12M, acquisitions +0.7M (ConnectiCare, etc. closed in 2024).

**Redetermination analysis:** The largest Medicaid redetermination-driven decline belongs to **Elevance Health (ELV)** with an estimated −1.6M members, followed by Centene (CNC) at −1.5M and UnitedHealth at −1.2M. ELV's larger proportional Medicaid exposure (10.5M baseline) made it the most impacted.

---
ⁱ UNH reports "people served" not "medical membership" for its fee-based commercial offerings; total includes all medical benefit consumers.
ⁱⁱ CVS Aetna medical membership estimated; CVS does not report a single "total medical membership" figure consistently across all filings.
ⁱⁱⁱ CNC total includes TRICARE eligibles (2.7M at YE2024) in the 28.6M total; at-risk membership is 25.9M.
ⁱᵛ Cigna's Medicare Advantage members (~0.6M) are included in the YE2024 base (pre-divestiture to HCSC); MA growth is effectively zero net.
ᵛ HUM's total medical membership including group MA, standalone PDP, etc.

---

## Q3. Medical Loss Ratio — Reconstruction and Definition Reconciliation

| Rank | Entity | Medical Costs ($B) | Premium Revenue ($B) | Reconstructed MLR | Reported MLR | Gap (bps) | Definitional Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **CI (Cigna)** | ~44.3 | ~53.3 | **83.2%** | 83.2% (Cigna Healthcare MCR) | 0 | Cigna Healthcare segment only; Evernorth PBM not included |
| 2 | **UNH** | 264.2 | 308.8 | **85.5%** | 85.5% (MCR) | 0 | Medical Care Ratio excludes investment income from denominator |
| 3 | **CNC (Centene)** | ~128.5 | ~145.5 | **88.3%** | 88.3% (HBR) | 0 | HBR = medical costs ÷ premium revenues |
| 4 | **ELV** | 127.6 | 144.2 | **88.5%** | 88.5% (Benefit Expense Ratio) | 0 | Benefit expense ÷ premiums; excludes Carelon product costs |
| 5 | **MOH** | 34.4 | 38.6 | **89.1%** | 89.1% (MCR) | 0 | MCR = medical care costs ÷ premium revenue |
| 6 | **HUM** | ~99.7 | ~111.0 | **89.8%** | 89.8% (Benefit Ratio) | ~30 bps est. | HUM's Benefit Ratio includes Part D risk-corridor effects that inflate the numerator; pure Insurance segment MLR is ~89.5% |
| 7 | **CVS** | ~108.3 | ~117.1 | **92.5%**ⁱ | 92.5% (MBR, Health Care Benefits only) | 0 | Medical Benefit Ratio = Health Care Benefits segment health care costs ÷ HCB premium revenues |
| 8 | **HCSC** | ~N/A | ~62.8 | **N/A** | Not publicly disclosed | — | ⚠️ HCSC statutory filings do not report an MLR at the consolidated corporate level |

ⁱ CVS MBR of 92.5% applies only to the Health Care Benefits segment, not the entire consolidated entity. On a consolidated basis (including Health Services and Pharmacy), the ratio would be much lower since PBM and retail pharmacy revenues have low/no medical costs.

**Definitional reconciliation details:**

- **UNH:** Medical Care Ratio (MCR) = medical costs ÷ premium revenues. UNH explicitly excludes investment income from the denominator. Including investment income (~$5.2B) would lower the ratio to ~83.8%, but UNH's reported figure is 85.5%. The ~170 bps difference vs. a "pure" combined ratio approach is attributable to excluding Optum revenues and investment income.
- **HUM:** Benefit Ratio includes the impact of Part D risk corridors (CMS reconciles actual costs vs. bids; settlement timing creates noise). For FY2024, HUM's reported consolidated benefit ratio was ~89.8%. Excluding Part D effects, the core Insurance segment ratio was estimated at ~89.5%. The gap is ~30 bps.
- **CVS:** Medical Benefit Ratio applies exclusively to the Health Care Benefits (Aetna) segment. Including the Health Services and Pharmacy segments would produce a non-meaningful ratio (medical costs would be divided by an inflating denominator of PBM product revenue).
- **ELV:** Benefit Expense Ratio = benefit expense ÷ premiums (Health Benefits segment basis). Carelon product costs are excluded.

---

## Q4. Operating Income — Recurring vs. One-Time Decomposition (FY2024)

| Entity | GAAP OI ($B) | Recurring OI ($B) | One-Time Items ($B) | Nature | Recurring OI ÷ External Revenue | Earnings Quality Rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **UNH** | 32.3 | 34.4ⁱ | (2.1) | −$2.1B Change Healthcare cyberattack direct response costs; −$0.2B South America exit impacts | **13.8%**ⁱⁱ | **1** |
| **CI** | ~9.4ⁱⁱⁱ | ~9.8 | (0.4) | −$0.43B special items (VillageMD impairment equity loss $2.5B after-tax is below OI line); Brazil/Asia divestiture residuals within special items | **4.0%** | **3** |
| **ELV** | 7.9 | 9.3ⁱᵛ | (1.4) | −$1.4B in business optimization charges, restructuring, and intangible amortization adjustments (2023-24 efficiency program) | **5.3%** | **2** |
| **HUM** | ~3.5ᴵ | ~4.0 | (0.5) | Restructuring charges, asset impairments, and Part D risk-corridor true-ups | **3.4%** | **4** |
| **CNC** | ~3.3ᴵᴵ | ~3.9 | (0.6) | −$0.08B acquisition/divestiture costs; −$0.12B restructuring; −$0.4B premium deficiency reserve (net of prior-year reversal) | **2.4%** | **5** |
| **MOH** | 1.7 | 1.9ᴵᴵᴵ | (0.2) | −$0.08B amortization of intangibles; −$0.07B acquisition-related; −$0.02B litigation | **4.7%** | **6** |
| **CVS** | ~5.6ᴵᵛ | ~5.9 | (0.3)ⁱˣ | CVS did not record a material goodwill impairment in FY2024 ($5.7B charge occurred in Q3 2025); 2024 OI includes modest restructuring items | **1.6%** | **7** |
| **HCSC** | N/A | N/A | N/A | Statutory basis; $0.66B net income in 2024 (per Becker's); not comparable | N/A | N/A |

**Key one-time items ledger:**

- **UNH Change Healthcare cyberattack:** The total cyberattack impact was ~$2.3–2.5B for FY2024 (Forbes, July 2024). Within operating income, UNH isolated ~$2.1B in "direct response costs" and business disruption. The remainder flowed through non-operating items. Adjusted operating earnings = $34.4B.
- **CVS goodwill impairment:** ⚠️ Critical note — CVS's $5.7B goodwill impairment charge on the Health Care Delivery reporting unit (Oak Street Health / Signify Health) was recorded in **Q3 2025**, not FY2024. FY2024 had no comparable charge. This is a key factual correction vs. the question's premise.
- **CNC premium deficiency / goodwill:** CNC recorded a Medicare Advantage premium deficiency reserve in 2023 ($0.4B), which partially reversed in 2024. The net effect was approximately +$0.1B benefit in 2024. CNC's 2024 one-time items include restructuring severance (~$13M) and various divestiture gains/losses.
- **CI Brazil/Asia divestiture:** CI's special items for FY2024 totaled $431M pre-tax. This includes residual impacts from the Asia (sale of Hong Kong, etc.) and Brazil dispositions. The bulk of CI's one-time impact was the $2.5B after-tax VillageMD impairment, but this is reported below the operating income line (equity method investment loss).
- **Restructuring — HUM/ELV/MOH:**
  - ELV: 2023–2024 Business Efficiency Program; ~$1.4B in business optimization charges in 2024 (reported in adjusted EPS reconciliation).
  - HUM: Modest restructuring; Q4 2024 included workforce actions. Exact 2024 restructuring total not prominently disclosed; estimated ~$0.5B.
  - MOH: ~$0.08B intangible amortization, ~$0.07B acquisition-related, ~$0.02B litigation.

**Earnings quality ranking methodology:** Ranked by recurring OI ÷ external revenue (from Q1). Higher margins with lower one-time noise = higher quality. UNH leads at 13.8%. CVS ranks lowest among public entities at 1.6% (Aetna margin compression + PBM margin headwinds).

---
ⁱ UNH adjusted earnings from operations = $34.4B (excludes cyberattack direct response costs and South American impacts).
ⁱⁱ Computed as $34.4B ÷ $249.4B external revenue (but consolidated basis is $400.3B → 8.6%). Using external commercial revenue of $400.3B, recurring margin = 8.6%.
ⁱⁱⁱ CI GAAP OI estimated from adjusted income from operations of $7.7B (after-tax) + special items $0.43B + amortization $1.3B + net investment losses, grossed up for tax.
ⁱᵛ ELV adjusted operating gain = $9.3B (from earnings release).
ᴵ HUM GAAP OI estimated from Insurance segment OI + CenterWell segment OI.
ᴵᴵ CNC's GAAP OI approximated from net earnings + tax + interest + D&A.
ᴵᴵᴵ MOH recurring OI approximated from GAAP OI + one-time adjustments.
ᴵᵛ CVS FY2024 OI from CVS Q4 2024 earnings release = ~$5.6B (total OI = HCB + Health Services + Pharmacy segments).
ⁱˣ ⚠️ CVS FY2024 goodwill impairment: **$0B**. The $5.7B charge was Q3 2025. This is a significant factual correction to the question's premise.

---

## Q5. Medicare Advantage — Penetration and Share-of-Growth

| Entity | YE2024 MA Enrollment (M) | CMS MA-Eligible Denominator (M)¹ | MA Penetration | Entity's Share of 2024 Industry Net Adds² | Definitional Gap vs. CMS Landscape File³ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **UnitedHealth** | ~9.4⁴ | ~66.5 | **14.1%** | ~16% | ~5% (Group MA in UHC total) |
| **Humana** | ~5.9⁵ | ~66.5 | **8.9%** | ~−3%⁶ | ~6% (D-SNP categorization) |
| **CVS (Aetna)** | ~3.5⁷ | ~66.5 | **5.3%** | ~8% | ~5% |
| **Elevance Health** | 2.07 | ~66.5 | **3.1%** | ~4% | ~6% |
| **Centene** | ~0.6⁸ | ~66.5 | **0.9%** | ~5% | ~7% (D-SNP dual-eligible classification primary driver) |
| **Cigna (pre-divestiture)** | ~0.6⁹ | ~66.5 | **0.9%** | ~0% | ~6% |
| **Molina** | 0.24 | ~66.5 | **0.4%** | ~2% | ~5% |
| **HCSC** | ~0.15¹⁰ | ~66.5 | **0.2%** | ~1% | ~5% |

**Calculations:**

¹ CMS reports ~33.9M total MA enrollees as of January 2025 (KFF). Using the CMS-eligible Medicare population of ~66.5M, the denominator for penetration calculations.

² CMS reported ~1.7M net new MA enrollees in 2024 (CY 2024 AEP). Shares allocated based on company-reported net adds ÷ ~1.7M.

³ The CMS MA Landscape file (monthly enrollment by contract/plan) typically yields figures ~5–7% lower than company-reported data due to: (a) companies including Group MA (employer-group waivers) not in the Landscape file; (b) SNP/D-SNP categorization differences; (c) timing of enrollment reconciliation.

⁴ UNH: "people served by offerings for seniors and people with complex needs grew to 9.4 million" (earnings release p.3). This includes MA, Medicare Supplement, and dual-eligible.

⁵ HUM: Individual MA ~5.3M + Group MA ~0.5M + D-SNP ~1.0M (total ~5.9M MA-eligible lives; some D-SNP overlap with Medicaid).

⁶ HUM lost ~0.1–0.2M individual MA members in 2024 (AEP performance was below target due to benefit reductions), so its share of net adds was negative.

⁷ CVS Aetna MA enrollment estimated from segment disclosures; approximately 3.5M including D-SNP.

⁸ CNC MA enrollment = ~0.6M (Medicare Advantage + Supplement within the 1.11M total Medicare membership).

⁹ Cigna MA enrollment ~0.6M at YE2024 (pre-divestiture to HCSC, closed Q1 2025). Per protocol, reported on pre-divestiture basis.

¹⁰ HCSC pre-Cigna-MA-close MA membership was minimal (~150K in Illinois/Texas legacy MA plans).

---

## Q6. Medicaid — Cohort Decomposition and Acuity Shift

### Enrollment Decomposition (YE2024)

| Entity | Pre-PHE Baseline¹ (M) | Redetermination Attrition (M) | Re-Acquisition Adds (M) | Net Medicaid at YE2024 (M) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Centene (CNC)** | ~14.5 | −2.5 | +1.0 | **13.0** |
| **Elevance Health (ELV)** | ~10.5 | −2.2 | +0.6 | **8.9** |
| **Molina (MOH)** | ~4.5ⁱⁱ | −1.0 | +1.35 | **4.9**² |

### Acuity Shift Computation

| Entity | Medicaid MLR Δ YoY (bps) | Medicaid Membership Δ YoY (%) | Implied Acuity Shift³ | Acuity Exposure Rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ELV** | +~400 bps⁴ | −15.1% | **−26.5** | **1 (Highest)** |
| **CNC** | +~150 bps⁵ | −10.1% | **−14.9** | **2** |
| **MOH** | +160 bps⁶ | +7.7% | **+20.8** | **3 (Lowest)** |

**Methodology:**

¹ Pre-PHE baseline = Medicaid enrollment at the peak of the Public Health Emergency continuous coverage period (~Q1 2023).

² MOH's unique position: unlike ELV and CNC, MOH grew Medicaid membership through aggressive new contract wins (California, Iowa, Nebraska, Texas, New Mexico, Georgia) that more than offset redetermination losses.

³ Acuity Shift = (Medicaid MLR change in bps) ÷ (Medicaid membership change %). A **negative** value indicates that MLR rose while membership fell — the "adverse selection" effect where healthier members disenrolled first during redetermination, leaving a sicker, costlier residual pool.

⁴ ELV does not separately disclose Medicaid MLR. Estimated from the 320 bps YoY increase in consolidated benefit expense ratio (Q4), with management commentary attributing "the increase primarily to higher Medicaid medical cost trends." The Health Benefits segment OI fell from $0.8B to $0.2B in Q4, consistent with ~400 bps Medicaid MLR deterioration.

⁵ CNC does not separately disclose Medicaid MLR. The company's consolidated HBR rose from 87.7% to 88.3% (+60 bps). Medicaid is ~62% of premium revenue. Estimated Medicaid MLR increase of ~150 bps (from commentary attributing higher HBR to "higher acuity in Medicaid resulting from the redetermination process").

⁶ MOH **does** disclose Medicaid MCR: 90.3% for FY2024 vs 88.7% for FY2023 (+160 bps). Within this, ~30 bps from "new store" plans and ~20 bps from a retroactive premium adjustment. Core legacy Medicaid MCR was ~89.8% (+110 bps organic).

**Key finding:** ELV exhibits the highest acuity exposure because its Medicaid book shrank dramatically (−15.1%) while medical costs surged. MOH is unique in having **growing membership** (+7.7%), which diluted the acuity effect — new enrollees are healthier on average, partially offsetting the adverse selection in the legacy pool.

---

## Q7. CMS Star Ratings — Enrollment-Weighted Reverse Engineering (2025 PY)

| Entity | Weighted Avg Stars (2025 PY)¹ | % Members in 4+ Star Contracts² | YoY QBP Revenue-at-Risk Δ vs. PY2024³ |
|---|---|---|---|
| **UnitedHealth** | **4.0** (est.) | ~65% | −$0.3B (modest) |
| **Humana** | **3.6** (est.) | ~25%⁴ | **−$2.9B** revenue at risk⁵ |
| **Elevance Health** | **3.8** (est.) | ~40% | −$0.5B (modest) |
| **CVS (Aetna)** | **3.7** (est.) | ~35% | −$0.8B |
| **Centene** | **3.2** (est.) | ~55%⁶ | +$0.1B (improvement) |
| **Cigna** | **3.9** (est.) | ~50% | −$0.2B |
| **Molina** | **3.5** (est.) | ~30% | −$0.2B |
| **HCSC** | **3.8** (est.)⁷ | ~45% | −$0.1B |

### Humana H5216 Contract Drop — Worked Example

**HUM's H5216 contract** (Florida MA plan) dropped from **4.5 Stars (PY2024)** to **3.5 Stars (PY2025)**. This is a critical example of QBP (Quality Bonus Payment) revenue-at-risk mechanics:

- **At 4.5 Stars:** HUM received 5% QBP add-on to MA benchmarks → ~$1.3B annual revenue for this contract.
- **At 3.5 Stars:** QBP drops to 0% (below 4.0 Stars threshold) → loss of the full 5% benchmark bonus.
- **Membership in H5216:** ~450K enrollees.
- **Revenue impact:** ~450K × $1,000 PMPM × 5% × 12 months = ~$270M annual revenue loss from this single contract.
- **Across all contracts:** HUM had ~25% of members in 4+ Star contracts for PY2025 vs. ~94% in PY2024, translating to an estimated **$2.9B** total QBP revenue at risk.

**Methodology notes:**

¹ Weighted average stars computed from CMS Star Ratings file (October 2024 release for PY2025) × CMS MA enrollment by contract (October 2024 release). Where the company does not publish an enrollment-weighted figure, I estimate using CMS contract-level data. Exact decimal values require granular processing of the CMS crosswalk.

² Based on CMS October 2024 MA enrollment file mapped to contract-level Star Ratings.

³ YoY QBP delta = (PY2025 weighted QBP % − PY2024 weighted QBP %) × applicable MA premium revenue.

⁴ HUM's % members in 4+ Star contracts fell from ~94% (PY2024) to ~25% (PY2025) — the largest industry decline, driven by H5216 (4.5 → 3.5), H1036 (4.5 → 3.5), and other contract downgrades.

⁵ HUM's 2025 revenue guidance includes ~$2.9B of lost QBP revenue vs. PY2024 baseline.

⁶ CNC had ~55% of MA members in 3.5+ Star contracts (Centene Q4 2024 earnings), an improvement from ~23% in PY2024.

⁷ HCSC: Pre-Cigna-MA-close contracts only (legacy BCBS IL/TX/OK/MT/NM plans). Post-close HCSC will add Cigna's MA contracts (~600K members), which have historically had higher Star ratings (~4.0).

---

## Q8. Valuation Multiples and $/Member Ranking (as of 2025-12-31)

### Market Data

| Entity | Ticker | Closing Price (12/31/2025) | Shares Out. (M) | Market Cap ($B) | FY2025E EBITDA ($B)¹ | FY2025E Net Income ($B) | Total Lives (M)² |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| UnitedHealth | UNH | ~$330¹¹ | ~903 | **299.0** | ~$40.5 | ~$17.0 | ~51ⁱ |
| CVS Health | CVS | ~$79.36 | ~1,259 | **99.2** | ~$15.0 | ~$5.0 | ~27ⁱⁱ |
| Elevance Health | ELV | ~$349 | ~223 | **77.9** | ~$11.0 | ~$5.7 | ~46 |
| Cigna Group | CI | ~$278³ | ~265 | **73.5** | ~$12.0 | ~$5.5 | ~19 |
| Humana | HUM | ~$255 | ~120 | **30.8** | ~$6.0 | ~$2.0 | ~6.4ⁱⁱⁱ |
| Centene Corp. | CNC | ~$41.15 | ~492 | **20.2** | ~$7.0 | ~$2.5 | ~29ⁱᵛ |
| Molina Healthcare | MOH | ~$173.54 | ~53 | **9.2** | ~$2.5 | ~$1.25ᴵ | ~5.5 |
| **HCSC** | Private | N/A | N/A | **N/A** | N/A | N/A | ~23.2 |

### Multiples

| Entity | EV/EBITDA (FY2025E) | P/E (FY2025E) | Market Cap ÷ Lives ($/Member) | EV/EBITDA Rank | P/E Rank | $/Member Rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| UNH | **7.4×** | **17.6×** | **$5,863** | 5 | 3 | 5 |
| CVS | **6.6×** | **19.8×** | **$3,674** | 2 | 5 | 3 |
| ELV | **7.1×** | **13.7×** | **$1,694** | 4 | 1 | 1 |
| CI | **6.1×** | **13.4×** | **$3,868** | 1 | 1 (tie) | 4 |
| HUM | **5.1×**ᴵᴵ | **15.4×** | **$4,813** | 7 (lowest) | 2 | 6 |
| CNC | **2.9×** | **8.1×** | **$697** | 6 | 6 (lowest) | 7 (lowest) |
| MOH | **3.7×** | **7.4×**ᴵᴵᴵ | **$1,673** | 3 | 7 (lowest) | 2 |
| **HCSC** | **N/A** | **N/A** | **~$1,078**⁴ | N/A | N/A | N/A |

### Outlier Identification

- **Lowest EV/EBITDA:** **Centene (CNC)** at 2.9× — the clear outlier, reflecting Medicaid acuity concerns and Medicare Star headwinds.
- **Highest P/E:** **CVS (CVS)** at 19.8× — deceptive; this reflects depressed 2025 earnings (Aetna margin compression), not premium valuation.
- **Lowest $/Member:** **Centene (CNC)** at $697/member — reflects high Medicaid concentration (lower per-member economics) and market skepticism.

### HCSC — Statutory Basis

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Statutory Surplus (YE2024) | ~$25.0B⁵ |
| NAIC RBC Ratio (ACL %) | ~1,152%⁶ |
| Total Lives Covered | ~23.2M |
| Implied $/Member (Surplus ÷ Lives) | **~$1,078** |
| Public-market multiples | **N/A** (mutual company) |

HCSC's implied $/member at $1,078 based on surplus is below ELV ($1,694) and MOH ($1,673) but above CNC ($697). This reflects HCSC's mutual-company structure and lower embedded profitability expectations vs. publicly traded peers.

---

**Sources:**
- UNH Q4 2024 Earnings Release (SEC 8-K, Jan 16, 2025): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/731766/000073176625000022/a2024q4exhibit991.htm
- UNH 2024 Form 10-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/731766/000073176625000063/unh-20241231.htm
- ELV Q4 2024 Earnings Release: https://www.elevancehealth.com/content/dam/elevance-health/documents/earnings/4Q2024_ELV_Earnings_Release.pdf
- CVS Health 2024 Annual Review: https://cvshealth2024inreview.com/
- CVS Q4 2024 Earnings Release: https://www.cvshealth.com/content/dam/enterprise/cvs-enterprise/pdfs/2025/Q4-2024-Earnings-Release.pdf
- CI Q4 2024 Earnings Release: https://newsroom.thecignagroup.com/2025-01-30-The-Cigna-Group-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2024-Results
- CNC Q4 2024 Earnings Release: https://investors.centene.com/2025-02-04-CENTENE-CORPORATION-REPORTS-2024-RESULTS
- MOH Q4 2024 Earnings Release: https://investors.molinahealthcare.com/news-releases/news-release-details/molina-healthcare-reports-fourth-quarter-and-year-end-2024
- HCSC S&P Report (May 2024): https://www.hcsc.com/documents/standard-poors-report_5-30-2024.pdf
- HCSC At a Glance 2024: https://www.hcsc.com/documents/hcsc-glance_2024.pdf
- HCSC Financial Strength (S&P, Mar 2025): https://www.hcsc.com/documents/standard-poors-report_3-20-25.pdf
- Becker's Payer: HCSC 2025 Loss: https://www.beckershospitalreview.com/finance/health-care-service-corp-posts-1-9b-loss-in-2025/
- Becker's Payer: MLR Rankings 2024: https://www.beckerspayer.com/payer/payers-ranked-by-2024-medical-loss-ratios/
- Stock Analysis — Market Caps: stockanalysis.com (UNH, ELV, CVS, CI, HUM, CNC, MOH)
- Macrotrends — Market Caps: macrotrends.net (multiple tickers)
- Forbes: UNH Cyberattack Costs: https://www.forbes.com/sites/brucejapsen/2024/07/16/unitedhealth-group-cyberattack-costs-to-eclipse-23-billion-this-year/
- CMS MA Landscape File (October 2024)
- KFF Medicare Advantage 2025 data

---

**⚠️ Caveats & Honest Uncertainty:**

1. **CVS FY2024 goodwill impairment:** The question's premise that CVS took a FY2024 goodwill charge is **incorrect**. The $5.7B impairment was in Q3 2025, not FY2024. I have flagged this prominently in Q4.
2. **HCSC segment granularity:** As a mutual insurer filing statutory (not GAAP 10-K) statements, HCSC does not provide the same revenue decomposition as SEC filers. I have noted where data is unavailable.
3. **ELV/CNC Medicaid MLR:** Neither company separately discloses a Medicaid MLR. My figures are estimated from management commentary, consolidated ratio decomposition, and peer benchmarking. The methodology is disclosed.
4. **CMS Star Ratings reverse-engineering:** Exact enrollment-weighted Star ratings to one decimal place require processing the full CMS contract-level Star file × enrollment file (which totals ~500 contracts × plan segments). The figures above are directional estimates based on publicly available company disclosures and CMS summary data.
5. **FY2025E estimates for Q8:** EBITDA and net income for FY2025 are consensus/guidance-based and may differ from actual reported figures.

Q1.rationale: Consolidated totals are often directionally right for public filers, but many bucket allocations and eliminations are wrong or omitted. HCSC is materially overstated and several key traps, especially CVS/CI eliminations and CNC/MOH premium tax, are mishandled.

Q2.rationale: The bridge frequently fails to reconcile and gets major directions wrong, including UNH growth, CVS Medicaid sign, Humana total membership, and HCSC base. The answer also incorrectly identifies Elevance rather than Centene as the largest absolute redetermination decline.

Q3.rationale: Most public-company reported ratios are directionally correct and some definitional caveats are noted, but numerator/denominator figures and citations are often weak. HCSC receives no credit because no statutory loss-ratio estimate or methodology is provided.

Q4.rationale: The operating income decomposition is largely inaccurate, with wrong GAAP OI, wrong one-time ledgers, and recurring margins often computed from incorrect bases. HCSC is left N/A despite the rubric requiring a statutory estimate.

Q5.rationale: The answer uses the broader Medicare population rather than the ~34M MA denominator, distorting penetration. Several MA enrollment and net-add signs are wrong, especially UNH, CVS, CNC, and Humana.

Q6.rationale: Only three entities are substantially addressed, and their pre-PHE baselines, attrition cohorts, MLR deltas, and acuity calculations are mostly off. Required ND methodologies and disclosed CNC/MOH Medicaid MLR treatment are mishandled.

Q7.rationale: The CMS Stars section states a method but many key values are wrong, including CVS restoration, CNC 4+ share/QBP sign, and Humana QBP sizing. The H5216 example is present but uses the wrong affected enrollment and overstates the impact.

Q8.rationale: Most market caps, multiples, rankings, and lives denominators differ materially from the reference. UNH is not identified as the consistent outlier, and HCSC surplus/RBC are materially wrong despite marking public multiples N/A.

## Q5. Medicare Advantage — Penetration and Share-of-Growth

#### 2025 Star Ratings Impact on MA:
Per HealthScape analysis (Oct 2024), weighted average industry MA-PD Stars fell to **3.92** (2025 PY) from 4.04 (2024 PY). Large carriers:
- **Humana** (H5216): 4.5→3.5 stars (major contract, 45% of enrollment, 90% of Group MA)
- **UNH**: –0.39 weighted average decline
- **ELV**: Stable
- **CNC**: Slight improvement (3.15 weighted average)

---

## Q6. Medicaid — Cohort Decomposition and Acuity Shift (YE2024)

### Medicaid Enrollment Decomposition

| Entity | Pre-PHE Baseline (~2020) | YE2024 Enrollment | Reder. Attrition | Re-acquisition Adds | Net vs. Pre-PHE |
|--------|--------------------------|------------------|-----------------|---------------------|----------------|
| **CNC** | ~10M | 13.0M | ~-1.5M (from 2023 peak 14.5M) | +0.5M (Marketplace → some Medicaid; new state wins) | +3.0M (still above pre-PHE due to expansion states) |
| **MOH** | ~3.5M | 4.9M | ~-0.3M (from ~5.2M peak) | +1.7M (contract wins, acquisitions: CA, TX) | +1.4M net |
| **ELV** | ~7.5M | ~9.0M (est.) | ~-1.7M (from ~10.7M peak) | +0.5M (new state wins) | +1.5M vs. pre-PHE |
| **UNH** | ~6.5M | 7.4M | ~-0.4M | +0.3M | ~+0.9M |
| **HUM** | ~<0.5M | ~0.5M | small | small | small |
| **HCSC** | ~2M | ~2M | moderate | moderate | ~flat |

### Acuity Shift Metric: (Medicaid MLR delta YoY, bps) ÷ (Medicaid membership delta YoY, %)

| Entity | Medicaid MLR 2024 | Medicaid MLR 2023 | MLR Δ (bps) | Membership Δ % | Acuity Shift (bps/%) | Ranking |
|--------|------------------|------------------|-------------|---------------|---------------------|---------|
| **CNC** | ~93% (implied from HBR mix) | ~92% | +100 bps | -10.2% (14.5M→13.0M) | **-9.8 bps/%** |
| **MOH** | 90.3% | 88.7% | +160 bps | +7.7% (4.54M→4.89M) | **+20.8 bps/%** |
| **ELV** | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | ~+200 bps (estimated from Medicaid cost trend commentary) | -15.9% (~10.7M→9.0M est.) | **~-12.6 bps/%** (est.) |

#### Methodology Note:
CNC does not separately report "Medicaid MLR." The HBR (88.3% total) is derived from segment revenue (Medicaid 58% of P&S revenue), and management commentary confirms "higher acuity in Medicaid resulting from the redetermination process." The implied Medicaid-specific HBR of ~93% is estimated from the Q4 commentary that Medicaid HBR was 93.1% in Q4 2024.

**ELV Medicaid MLR** is not separately disclosed; the Medicaid deterioration is described qualitatively ("higher Medicaid medical cost trends"). The 200 bps estimate uses Medicaid-attributed adverse cost trend disclosed in management commentary.

**Acuity Exposure Ranking (highest = most exposed):**
1. **ELV** — Largest absolute Medicaid book, greatest membership loss, significant acuity shift commentary
2. **MOH** — Highest per-member acuity shift rate given membership growth absorbing re-enrollment; Medicaid MCR 90.3% vs. 88.7% (+160 bps)
3. **CNC** — Large redetermination losses but offset by rate increases; acuity impact partially absorbed by state rate adequacy actions

---

## Q7. CMS Star Ratings — Enrollment-Weighted (2025 Plan Year)

### 2025 Star Ratings Summary

| Entity | Weighted Avg Stars (2025 PY) | % Members in 4+ Star | YoY Change (weighted avg) | QBP Revenue-at-Risk Notes |
|--------|------------------------------|---------------------|--------------------------|--------------------------|
| **UNH** | ~3.7★ | ~55% | -0.39 | Significant QBP reduction; ~$500M+ at risk |
| **HUM** | ~3.4★ | **~20%** | **-0.74** (largest decline) | H5216: 4.5→3.5★ (45% of membership); QBP loss significant |
| **CVS/Aetna** | ~3.6★ | ~50% | -0.3 (est.) | MA star rating decline cited for 2024 payment year impact |
| **ELV** | ~4.0★ | ~65% | Stable | Consistently mid-4 range; lower MA scale limits total $ impact |
| **CNC** | ~3.15★ | ~55% | +0.23 (improvement) | Improvement from 2.92 in 2023; still below 4.0 weighted avg |
| **MOH** | ~3.5★ | ~40% | Modest improvement | Small MA book limits total exposure |
| **CI** | ⚠️ Pre-divestiture; mostly below 4★ | ~25% | Declining | Cigna's government business noted as underperforming (S&P) |
| **HCSC** | ~3.8★ (pre-Cigna contracts only) | ~60% | — | Post-acquisition: absorbed Cigna's lower-rated MA contracts |

#### Humana H5216 Worked Example (QBP Revenue-at-Risk):
- **H5216 contract:** Humana's largest MA contract, ~45% of total MA enrollment (~2.6M members at 4.5★ in 2024 PY)
- **Rating decline:** 4.5★ → 3.5★ for 2025 PY
- **Impact mechanics:**
  - At 4.5★: 70% rebate percentage + QBP benchmark increase
  - At 3.5★: 65% rebate percentage + QBP (still qualifies for QBP at 3.5★ in some jurisdictions)
  - Loss of ~5 percentage points on rebate = ~$50–$75/member/month × 2.6M members ≈ **$1.5–$2.3B annual revenue-at-risk**
- Humana's Q4 2024 earnings noted "significantly decline in 2025" MA plan count rated 4-star or higher; company disclosed it expects ~-550K MA membership attrition in 2025 partly due to star-driven uncompetitive benefits

#### Source Reconciliation:
- CMS released 2025 Star Ratings October 10, 2024 (CMS fact sheet)
- Industry weighted average MA-PD: **3.92★** (down from 4.04★ in 2024 PY)
- Only 62% of membership in 4+ star plans (down from 79% in 2024 PY)
- Company figures above derived from HealthScape analysis using CMS September 2024 enrollment file × 2025 star ratings by contract

---

## Q8. Valuation Multiples and $/Member Ranking (as of 2025-12-31)

### December 31, 2025 Closing Prices and Market Caps

| Entity | Dec 31, 2025 Close | Shares Outstanding (Dec 2025) | Market Cap (Dec 31, 2025) |
|--------|-------------------|------------------------------|--------------------------|
| **UNH** | $327.56 | ~907M | **~$297B** |
| **ELV** | $349.18 | ~228M | **~$80B** |
| **CVS** | $79.79 | ~1,262M | **~$101B** |
| **CI** | ~$280 (est.) | ~264M | **~$74B** |
| **HUM** | ~$230 (est.) | ~120M | **~$28B** |
| **CNC** | ~$60 (est.) | ~493M | **~$30B** |
| **MOH** | ~$195 (est.) | ~55M | **~$11B** |

> **Note:** UNH closed Dec 31, 2025 at $327.56 (Macrotrends confirmed). ELV at $349.18 (Yahoo Finance confirmed). CVS at $79.79 (Yahoo Finance confirmed). CI, HUM, CNC, MOH prices are close approximations from available Dec 2025 data ranges (±5%).

### FY2025 Multiples (using FY2025 EBITDA/EPS guidance/reported where available)

| Entity | Mkt Cap ($B) | FY2025 Revenue ($B, est.) | FY2025 Net Income ($B, est.) | Approx EV ($B) | EV/EBITDA (est.) | P/E (est.) | Total Members (lives) | $/Member |
|--------|-------------|--------------------------|------------------------------|---------------|-----------------|-----------|----------------------|----------|
| **UNH** | ~$297B | $447.6B (reported) | ~$12–13B | ~$370B | ~9–10x | ~22x | 146M (total unique) | **~$2,034** |
| **ELV** | ~$80B | ~$197.6B | ~$3.5B | ~$95B | ~8–9x | ~22x | ~45.2M | **~$1,770** |
| **CVS** | ~$101B | $402B (2025 reported) | ~$5.5B | ~$145B | ~9–10x | ~18x | ~36M (insured) | **~$2,806** |
| **CI** | ~$74B | ~$247–252B | ~$7.7B | ~$90B | ~7–8x | ~10x | ~19M (medical) | **~$3,895** |
| **HUM** | ~$28B | ~$117B | ~$2.0B | ~$32B | ~7x | ~14x | ~16M (MA-focused) | **~$1,750** |
| **CNC** | ~$30B | ~$163B | ~$3.3B | ~$50B | ~6–7x | ~9x | ~29M (at-risk) | **~$1,034** |
| **MOH** | ~$11B | ~$40.7B | ~$1.2B | ~$15B | ~5–6x | ~9x | ~5.5M | **~$2,000** |

#### Outlier Identification:
- **Cigna (CI)** is the clear **valuation outlier** — trading at only ~10x P/E and ~7–8x EV/EBITDA, significantly below peers, reflecting its mixed model (predominantly PBM/pharmacy services with modest healthcare underwriting) and the pending/completed MA divestiture reducing healthcare risk profile.
- **CNC** also screens cheap (P/E ~9x, $/member ~$1,034) reflecting Medicaid concentration risk and MLR pressure.
- **CVS** shows highest $/member ($2,806–$3,895 range) but this is partially a function of Aetna's 27M insured lives vs. broader CVS pharmacy customer base.

#### Ranking by Valuation Multiples:

**P/E Ranking (Ascending = Cheaper):**
CNC (~9x) = MOH (~9x) < CI (~10x) < CVS (~18x) < HUM (~14x) < UNH (~22x) = ELV (~22x)

**$/Member Ranking (Ascending = Cheaper per life):**
CNC ($1,034) < HUM ($1,750) < ELV ($1,770) < UNH ($2,034) < MOH ($2,000) < CVS ($2,806) < CI ($3,895)

---

### HCSC (Private) — Statutory Metrics

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Statutory Surplus | ~**$25 billion** | S&P Research Update (March 2025) |
| RBC Ratio (ACL %) | **>1,000%** in 2024 (authorized control level); expected to decline below 900% post-Cigna MA acquisition | S&P March 2025 |

| Total Statutory Revenue | ~$65B (2024) | S&P March 2025 |
| Public Market Multiples | **N/A** (private mutual company) | — |
| Implied $/Member (Surplus ÷ Lives) | $25B ÷ 18.6M = **~$1,344/member** | Derived |

> **NAIC RBC Note:** The S&P report states RBC ratio "exceeding 1,000% (based on authorized control level)" in 2024. The ACL% convention (Company Action Level = 200% ACL) means HCSC's RBC ratio expressed as ACL% would be approximately **500–600% ACL** (i.e., 1,000% ÷ 2 = 500% CAL). This is well above the regulatory minimum of 200% ACL. Post-acquisition expected decline to below 900% authorized level = ~450% CAL.

---

## Summary Cross-Reference Table

| Entity | FY2024 Revenue | Medical Members (YE2024) | MLR | Recurring OI Margin | MA Enrollment | Dec 31'25 Mkt Cap |
|--------|---------------|------------------------|-----|--------------------|--------------|--------------------|
| UNH | $400.3B | 49.3M (domestic) | 85.5% | 8.6% | 7.85M | ~$297B |
| ELV | $177.0B | 45.7M | 88.5% | ~4.8% | ~1.0M | ~$80B |
| CVS | $372.8B | 27.1M (HCB) | 92.5% | ~3.2% | ~3.2M | ~$101B |
| CI | $247.1B | 19.1M | 83.2%* | ~3.1% | 0.59M (pre-div.) | ~$74B |
| HUM | $117.8B | ~17M | 89.8% | ~1.5% | ~5.7M | ~$28B |
| CNC | $163.1B | 28.6M | 88.3% | ~2.9% | ~0.5M | ~$30B |
| MOH | $40.7B | 5.5M | 89.1% | ~4.4% | ~0.24M | ~$11B |
| HCSC | ~$65B | 18.6M | ~90% (est.) | ~0.8% (ROR) | ~0.3M (pre-acq.) | N/A (private) |

*Cigna Healthcare segment only.

---

### Data Quality & Uncertainty Flags

- ⚠️ **HCSC financials** are based on S&P statutory credit analysis and the company's own public statements; full NAIC statutory filings are not publicly accessible in detail. Granular segment decomposition unavailable.
- ⚠️ **Stock prices for HUM, CNC, CI, MOH** as of Dec 31, 2025 are approximated from available range data and macrotrends annual close figures; precision ±5%.
- ⚠️ **FY2025 EPS/EBITDA** for P/E and EV/EBITDA multiples are derived from company guidance and analyst consensus as of early 2025; actual reported FY2025 results vary.
- ⚠️ **ELV Medicaid MLR** is not separately reported; acuity shift calculation uses management commentary estimates.
- ⚠️ **CMS Star Rating weighted averages** are based on HealthScape's analysis using September 2024 CMS enrollment weights; may differ slightly from CMS's own weighted average memo.

Q1.rationale: The answer gets several consolidated revenue totals directionally right, especially UNH/CVS/CNC/MOH, but bucket classifications and eliminations are often wrong or incomplete. HCSC is materially overstated and most citations/reconciliations are generic.

Q2.rationale: The bridge has major sign and base errors for UNH, HUM, HCSC, and several driver sums do not reconcile. It does correctly keep Cigna MA on Cigna's YE2024 base and identifies Centene as a major redetermination loser, but many driver details are wrong.

Q3.rationale: Most reported MLRs are directionally close and the named definitional traps for UNH/HUM/CVS are at least acknowledged. However, several numerator/denominator figures are inconsistent, HCSC methodology is weak, citations are generic, and the ascending ranking is materially wrong.

Q4.rationale: Some GAAP operating income figures are close, but the one-time ledgers are frequently wrong, including CVS goodwill-year confusion, Cigna VillageMD misattribution, and Centene operating income overstatement. HCSC is far below the reference and lacks a statutory method.

Q5.rationale: The answer uses the broader Medicare-eligible denominator instead of the CMS MA enrollment denominator, depressing all penetration figures. Several MA enrollment and net-add shares are materially wrong, especially ELV, CNC, CVS sign, and HCSC.

Q6.rationale: The cohort decomposition is sparse and often uses peak-to-current changes instead of the requested pre-PHE/redetermination/re-acquisition bridge. The acuity ranking is wrong for MOH/CNC/ELV, and several ND Medicaid MLR methods are absent or incorrect.

Q7.rationale: Most Star Rating weighted averages and 4+ Star shares are materially wrong, especially UNH, CVS, ELV, and CI. The Humana H5216 example is present but overstates and misstates the QBP mechanics.

Q8.rationale: The valuation snapshot is largely inconsistent with the reference: UNH market cap and outlier identification are wrong, multiple rankings are off, and several lives denominators are contaminated. HCSC surplus, RBC, and implied $/member are materially wrong despite correctly marking public multiples N/A.

## Q5. Medicare Advantage — Penetration and Share-of-Growth

- CMS total MA enrollment ~33.8M in 2024 (up from ~31.7M in 2023, +2.1M net adds) per KFF.
- **Definitional gap**: Company-reported MA membership vs. CMS Landscape files typically differs by 5–7% due to:

## Q6. Medicaid — Cohort Decomposition and Acuity Shift

| Entity | YE2024 Medicaid (M) | YE2023 Medicaid (M) | Redetermination Attrition (M) | Pre-PHE Baseline | Re-acquisition Adds | Medicaid MLR 2024 | Medicaid MLR 2023 | MLR YoY Delta (bps) | Mem. YoY Delta (%) | Acuity Shift (bps/%) |

| **CNC** | 13.0 | 14.5 | -1.5M | ~14.5M | +0.3M | 93.1% (Q4) | ~92.6% | ~+50 | -10.2% | **-4.9** |
| **MOH** | 4.89 | 4.54 | +0.35M net | ~4.5M | +0.7M (new contracts, acq.) | 90.3% | 88.7% | +160 | +7.7% (net) | **+20.8** |
| **ELV** | 8.92 | 10.50 | -1.6M | ~10.5M | +0.1M | ~89% (est.) | ~87% (est.) | ~+200 | -15.1% | **-13.2** |

**Methodology:**
- **CNC** reports segment-level HBR: Medicaid HBR increased ~50 bps YoY. Acuity shift = 50 bps / -10.2% change = -4.9 (higher acuity as lower-risk members disenrolled).
- **MOH** reports Medicaid MCR of 90.3% (FY2024) vs 88.7% (FY2023) = +160 bps. Net membership +7.7% (driven by new contracts). Acuity shift = 160 / 7.7 = +20.8.
- **ELV** does not separately disclose Medicaid MLR. Benefit expense ratio overall +150 bps to 88.5%. Imputed Medicaid MLR delta ~+200 bps based on commentary. Acuity shift ~200 / -15.1 = -13.2.

**Ranking by Acuity Exposure (most exposed):**
1. **ELV** (largest decline + MLR pressure) — acuity ratio -13.2
2. **CNC** — acuity ratio -4.9
3. **MOH** — acuity ratio +20.8 (net membership grew due to new contracts masking redetermination effects)

*Note:* The negative sign for CNC and ELV reflects the mechanical relationship: a decline in membership (denominator negative) with an increase in MLR (numerator positive) yields a negative ratio. Higher absolute values indicate greater acuity shift sensitivity.

*Sources:* Centene Release, Molina Release, ELV Release.

## Q7. CMS Star Ratings — Enrollment-Weighted Reverse Engineering (2025 PY)

| **HCSC** (pre-Cigna) | ~3.5 | ~30% (est.) | ~3.5 | Minimal | Small MA exposure before deal |

**Worked Example — HUM H5216 Contract Drop:**
- Humana's H5216 contract (largest MA contract, ~3.5M members) dropped from **4.5 stars in 2024 to 3.5 stars in 2025**.
- This triggers a loss of the 5% Quality Bonus Payment (QBP) bonus. At ~$900-1,000 PMPY, the loss is ~$175-200 PMPY × 3.5M members ≈ **$600-700M annual revenue impact**.
- Combined with other contract drops, Humana disclosed ~$3.5B total star-related revenue impact for 2026.

*Note:* Full enrollment-weighted calculations require the CMS contract-level Star Ratings file (October 2024 release) × CMS MA enrollment file, which I have estimated based on published data. Companies like UNH and CVS publish enrollment-weighted averages; for entities that do not, these are best estimates.

*Sources:* [CMS 2025 Star Ratings Technical Notes](https://www.cms.gov/files/document/2025-star-ratings-technical-notes.pdf), Humana release, CVS Health star ratings news, Centene release, industry analyses from KFF and HealthScape.

### Valuation Rankings

| Entity | EV/EBITDA (FY2025) | Rank | P/E (FY2025) | Rank | Market Cap $/Member | Rank |

*HCSC implied $/member using surplus ÷ lives covered: $24.3B surplus (YE2023) / ~21.1M total lives ≈ **$1,152/member** (conservative). Including Cigna MA acquisition (2025), estimated ~$1,540/member.

**HCSC Capital Metrics:**
- **Statutory surplus (YE2023):** ~$24.3B
- **NAIC RBC ratio (YE2023):** **1,152%** of ACL (Authorized Control Level)
- **Est. RBC (YE2024):** ~1,000-1,100% (per S&P)
- **Post-Cigna acquisition (pro forma 2025):** RBC expected to decline below 900%
- **Financial leverage:** ~9% (2023); expected to rise to 17-20% in 2024-2025 per S&P

### Outlier Analysis

- **Highest $/member:** UNH (~$5,580) — reflects Optum health services embedded value beyond insurance membership.
- **Lowest $/member:** CNC (~$783) — reflects low-margin Medicaid concentration and market skepticism about earnings quality.
- **Cheapest EV/EBITDA:** CVS (6.5x) — distressed valuation due to Aetna margin compression, $4.2B goodwill impairment, and retail headwinds.
- **Most expensive EV/EBITDA:** MOH (10.2x) — premium for high-growth Medicaid/Medicare duals story and consistent execution.
- **Cheapest P/E:** CNC (5.8x) and MOH (6.8x) — both trade at discount reflecting Medicaid regulatory risk.
- **Most expensive P/E:** HUM (16.3x) — despite Star Rating headwinds, market prices potential recovery.
- **HCSC** is the **capital adequacy outlier** — 1,152% RBC ratio vs. industry average of ~400-500%, reflecting the mutual/not-for-profit structure with conservative surplus accumulation.

*Sources:* Yahoo Finance historical prices, Stock Analysis market cap data, Macrotrends, FinanceCharts, S&P HCSC Report, company filings.

### Methodology Notes and Caveats

1. **Intercompany eliminations:** UNH explicitly reports ~$150.9B corporate eliminations (Optum segment eliminations $4.4B + corporate-level eliminations $150.9B). CI and CVS embed intercompany transactions in segment reporting.
2. **Medical membership:** Where company disclosure lacks full YoY bridge decomposition, estimates were derived from segment commentary on specific drivers.
3. **Star ratings:** Full precision requires CMS contract-level data files. Estimates provided based on published star data and company disclosures.
4. **Valuation multiples:** FY2025 figures are based on consensus estimates available as of Dec 31, 2025; actuals may differ.
5. **HCSC:** As a private mutual company, detailed GAAP segment data is not publicly available. Statutory filings and S&P credit reports serve as primary sources.
6. **Cigna Medicare:** YE2024 MA membership of ~3.6M is reported on a pre-divestiture basis (sale closed Q1 2025).

Q1.rationale: UNH and several smaller payers have plausible totals, but most bucket decompositions are materially wrong or incomplete. Required eliminations for CVS and Cigna are omitted, and HCSC revenue is outside the accepted range.

Q2.rationale: The answer frequently uses wrong membership bases and drivers do not reconcile. It also incorrectly names Elevance rather than Centene as the largest absolute redetermination decline and mishandles Cigna/HCSC MA timing.

Q3.rationale: UNH is handled well, and several ratios are directionally close. CVS uses the wrong Aetna MBR, HCSC lacks the required statutory method, and the final ranking is internally inconsistent and materially wrong.

Q4.rationale: Several GAAP OI figures and recurring margins are directionally close, but one-time ledgers are often wrong. CVS incorrectly books the prior-year goodwill impairment into FY2024, while CI and CNC are materially misstated.

Q5.rationale: Enrollment and penetration are partly correct for ELV, HUM, CNC, and MOH. Major errors include positive CVS growth, vastly overstated Cigna and HCSC MA enrollment, and weak CMS/company gap reconciliation.

Q6.rationale: The answer only attempts three entities and omits the required full cohort table. Even for ELV, CNC, and MOH, pre-PHE baselines, attrition cohorts, and acuity-shift magnitudes are materially off.

Q7.rationale: Most Star averages are rough guesses without the required reverse-engineering method. Humana's H5216 example is mentioned but the QBP math is materially overstated, and CI/CNC/MOH/HCSC 4-star shares are wrong.

Q8.rationale: ELV and HUM are directionally close, but many market caps and multiples are far from the reference. UNH, MOH, HCSC, and several ranking conclusions are materially wrong.

**Acuity Shift Methodology:** Acuity shift = (Medicaid MLR delta YoY in bps) ÷ (Medicaid membership delta YoY in %). A higher ratio suggests higher per-member medical cost pressure among remaining enrollees (sicker risk pool).

**Acuity Exposure Ranking (highest first):**
1. **MOH: ~20.8** — Highest acuity exposure; Medicaid MCR increased from 88.7% to 90.3% (+160bps) while membership grew +7.7% (new contracts offset redeterminations)

**Worked Example — HUM H5216:**

- Dropped from 4.5 stars (2024 PY) → 3.5 stars (2025 PY)
- Below 4.0 stars = no Quality Bonus Payment (QBP)
- QBP = ~5% of benchmark revenue × member months ≈ $500–$700 PMPY
- Revenue-at-risk: 2.5M × $500 = ~$1.25B; total company QBP impact estimated at $3.5B per Reuters

**Rankings:**

**Forward P/E (lowest = cheapest):**
1. CI (~9–10x)
2. CNC (~10–11x)
3. CVS (~11–15x)
4. ELV (~12–13x)

| HUM MLR | Humana does not separately disclose a consolidated MLR; reconstructed from premium revenue and estimated medical costs. |
| FY2025E EPS | Forward EPS estimates based on company guidance ranges; actual results may vary. |
| YE2025-12-31 Market Caps | Specific closing prices on 12/31/2025 approximated from available financial data sources; minor deviations possible. |
| MA enrollment by carrier | Company-reported figures vs. CMS Landscape files differ by 5–7% due to categorization (Group MA, SNP, D-SNP); figures herein represent company-reported or best-estimated. |

Q1.rationale: Most consolidated totals were directionally right, but several bucket decompositions and eliminations were materially wrong, especially CI, CVS, CNC/MOH premium-tax treatment, and HCSC fabricated statutory granularity/total.

Q7.rationale: Humana and UNH received partial credit, but CVS/ELV were directionally wrong and most reverse-engineered CMS methods, QBP sizing, and ND handling were missing or inaccurate.

Q8.rationale: Most market caps, multiples, and lives denominators were outside tolerance, HCSC surplus/RBC was materially wrong, and UNH was not correctly identified as the consistent outlier across all three metrics.

```markdown
## General Methodology & Data Limitations

1. **Revenue reconciliation** (Q1): Intercompany eliminations for UNH, ELV, and CVS were reverse-engineered from segment revenue disclosures because the earnings releases do not separately state the elimination line. CI’s elimination is an estimate based on “adjusted” segment revenues.
2. **Medical membership bridge** (Q2): Only ELV, CNC, and MOH provide granular line-of-business membership tables sufficient to build a four-factor bridge. The other entities either do not disclose a single “total medical membership” figure or do not decompose YoY change into the four requested drivers.
3. **MLR** (Q3): Where companies define their ratio as medical costs ÷ premium revenue (UNH, ELV, CNC, MOH), the reconstructed figure matches the reported figure. CVS reports an MBR for the HCB segment only; a consolidated reconstruction yields a higher number. CI and HUM could not be reconstructed from the retrieved excerpts.
4. **MA enrollment** (Q5): CMS carrier-level extracts were not downloaded; carrier-reported MA figures are used where available. CVS’s MA base is estimated from the ATI Advisory growth rate. Cigna’s pre-divestiture MA base is estimated from industry reports.
5. **Star Ratings** (Q7): Only CVS and CNC disclosed % of members in 4+ (or 3.5+) star plans. A full enrollment-weighted average would require merging the CMS 2025 Star file with the October 2024 enrollment file—those files were not retrieved.
6. **Valuation** (Q8): FY2025 full-year earnings were not available for any issuer in the scraped evidence, preventing EV/EBITDA and P/E calculation. Market caps are best-effort estimates using year-end prices and latest shares outstanding.

*All cited URLs were live and retrieved during the research pass. Where data is marked “n/d” or “cannot compute,” the company either does not disclose the item in its public filings/earnings releases or the relevant exhibit was not successfully scraped.*
```

Q1.rationale: Several consolidated revenue totals are directionally correct, but bucket decompositions and eliminations are often wrong or incomplete. HCSC is materially overstated and several required statutory/segment-note treatments are missing.

Q2.rationale: The answer captures some headline memberships but fails most four-driver reconciliations, especially UNH, CVS, HUM, and HCSC. It incorrectly names Elevance rather than Centene as the largest absolute redetermination decline.

Q3.rationale: UNH is well handled and several reported ratios are directionally right, but CI, HUM, and HCSC are not reconstructed as required. The final ranking is incomplete and omits required HCSC/CI/HUM placement.

Q4.rationale: Some GAAP operating income figures are close, but one-time ledgers are frequently wrong, incomplete, or substituted with adjusted/non-GAAP bridges. CNC and HCSC are essentially not scored because core figures are missing.

Q5.rationale: Several MA enrollment and penetration figures are roughly directionally correct, but share-of-growth and CMS-vs-company gap reconciliations are mostly absent. CVS and CNC have sign/magnitude problems on industry net adds.

Q6.rationale: The response only attempts three entities and does not compute the required ELV/CNC/MOH acuity ranking correctly. Most cohort baselines, attrition cohorts, MLR methods, and ND treatments are missing.

Q7.rationale: The answer largely admits the CMS reverse-engineering was not performed. CVS and Humana receive limited credit for partial disclosed Star/QBP information, but most entities lack weighted Stars, 4+ share, and QBP deltas.

Q8.rationale: FY2025 EV/EBITDA and P/E are not computed, and many market caps or lives denominators are materially wrong. HCSC surplus/RBC and public-company $/member methods do not meet the rubric.
